guards.issue: MECHANISM EV-4, one verdict at every FORCED site (rule 3). The sim does model the offer contract elsewhere -- Event.resume_after_combat RETURNS potions 'to surface as take-or-skip offers (RewardsCmd.OfferCustom)' (events/base.py:116-122), which is how battleworn_dummy hands its Setting1 potion to the driver -- so this is an inconsistency inside the sim, not a missing capability. Declining is a real choice: a colourless card reward can be a card the player does not want in the deck, and a potion offer can be declined to keep a belt slot for a later pick. The source distinguishes the two screens deliberately: BrainLeech's SHARE_KNOWLEDGE sets `Cancelable = false` on its grid pick (BrainLeech.cs:67-70) while its RIP branch uses plain OfferCustom (BrainLeech.cs:58). LIVE at every site listed, all of which are reachable event branches with no exotic gate.

guards.what: EV-2: ClimbOption's 13 Max HP loss (DrowningBeacon.cs:53) calls RunState.lose_max_hp (run.py:316-321), which floors max HP and CLAMPS current HP. C#'s CreatureCmd.LoseMaxHp (CreatureCmd.cs) damages the overflow through the damage pipeline (Unblockable|Unpowered) FIRST, against the UNFLOORED new max, and only then calls SetMaxHp(Math.Max(1m, newMaxHp))
guards.issue: MECHANISM EV-2, one verdict at every lose_max_hp site (rule 3). Two legs, both EXECUTED (`py audit/tools/event_probes.py maxhp`): (1) the overflow is real damage, so HP-loss modifiers apply -- at 80/80 losing 10 max HP with the ported Tungsten Rod relic the sim lands on 70 and the game on 71; (2) losing more max HP than the player has: the game computes the damage against the unfloored new max (80 - 100 = -20, so 100 damage) and kills the player, while the sim floors max HP at 1 first and leaves them alive at 1/1. LIVE on leg (1): Tungsten Rod is a ported relic (relics/tungsten_rod.py:39) and every max-HP-loss event is reachable with it held. Leg (2) needs a max-HP loss larger than the player's max HP, which no ported event amount reaches, so leg (2) alone is dormant.
